## site.read

Read the site record: its id, slug (the site part of its platform address, `<site>--<program>.<base domain>`), name, theme, blueprint, program, and the parent site and mount path when it is mounted under another site. site_context answers its languages and addresses.

- permission `site.read` (admin, editor); class `read`; writes nothing.
- Input: `{}`.

Output: { site: { id: string, slug: string, name: string, theme: string, blueprintId: string, programId?: string, parentSiteId?: string \| null, mountPath?: string \| null, domain?: string, createdAt: string, updatedAt: string } }

Example input:

```json
{}
```

## site.update

Rename the site, change its slug (lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens; a reserved slug is refused, one another site holds is 409 site_slug_exists) or mount it under another site of the same workspace at a path (`parentSiteId`, `mountPath`; null unmounts it). Undo restores the routing it changed.

- permission `site.admin` (admin); class `transaction`; writes `site`; undoable with `history.undo`.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string (min 1, max 255) |  |
| `slug` | string (min 1, max 100) |  |
| `parentSiteId` | string (min 1, max 36) \| null |  |
| `mountPath` | string (max 255) \| null |  |

Output: { site: { id: string, slug: string, name: string, theme: string, blueprintId: string, programId?: string, parentSiteId?: string \| null, mountPath?: string \| null, domain?: string, createdAt: string, updatedAt: string } }

Example input:

```json
{"name":"Studio site"}
```

## settings.read

Read the draft site settings, key by key: the theme's setting fields (`companyName`, `legalLine`, `supportEmail`, `logoWidth`, `socialImage`, `favicon`, the analytics and consent keys `analyticsProvider`, `analyticsSiteId`, `analyticsHost`, `consentPolicyVersion`, ...), `blockReveal` (the reveal every block of the page's sections, or the footer's, plays), `styleBreakpoints` (the list breakpoints.update replaces; absent while the site keeps the defaults), `redirects` (the list redirects.update replaces) and `notFoundPage` (the page settings.setNotFoundPage names).

- permission `site.read` (admin, editor); class `read`; writes nothing.
- Input: `{}`.

Output: { settings: Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<string, …>)[] \| Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<string, …>>> }

Example input:

```json
{}
```

## settings.update

Write site settings key by key: each key of the input replaces that setting and the others stay. The analytics and consent keys are checked together on the result (an unknown provider, a site id of the wrong shape is refused), and `blockReveal` against its contract (null clears it). `styleBreakpoints`, the layout frames, `redirects` and `notFoundPage` are refused here: use breakpoints.update, layout.update, redirects.update and settings.setNotFoundPage. Settings are versioned: the public site serves them after the next publish; undo restores the previous values.

- permission `site.edit` (admin, editor); class `transaction`; writes `settings`; undoable with `history.undo`.
- Input: `{}`.

Output: { settings: Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<string, …>)[] \| Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<string, …>>> }

Example input:

```json
{"siteTitle":"Studio"}
```

## settings.setNotFoundPage

Choose the page an address no page answers shows: `notFoundPage` is `{ pageId, locales? }`, `pageId` the page in every language and `locales` another page for a language (`{ "en": "<page id>" }`), or null for the theme's built-in "page not found". The public site then answers such an address with HTTP 404 (never a redirect) and that page's content in the address's language, marked noindex; the page's own address answers 404 the same way, and it is left out of the sitemap, the automatic page lists and search. Refused with 422 `not_found_page_invalid`, every problem named: a page that does not exist, is not a static page, is the home page, has pages under it, is members only or has a password, or a language the site does not have. The page shows publicly once it is published; settings are versioned, so the choice goes live with the next publish; undo restores the previous one.

- permission `site.edit` (admin, editor); class `transaction`; writes `settings`; undoable with `history.undo`.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `notFoundPage` | { pageId: string (min 1, max 36), locales?: Record<string, string (min 1, max 36)> } \| null | yes |

Output: { notFoundPage: { pageId: string (min 1, max 36), locales?: Record<string, string (min 1, max 36)> } \| null }

Example input:

```json
{"notFoundPage":{"pageId":"<page id>","locales":{"en":"<page id>"}}}
```

## breakpoints.update

Replace the site's style breakpoints, the ids `bp:<id>` scopes and component cells name. `styleBreakpoints` is the whole new list, mobile-first: `base` first, then each `{ id, label, minWidth, maxWidth?, condition? }` with min widths increasing (a breakpoint may hold only a media `condition` instead). `before` is the list as it is now (settings.read `styleBreakpoints`, or the defaults `base`, `sm` 480, `md` 768, `lg` 1024, `xl` 1440 when it is absent); another one is refused as changed elsewhere (409). The ids `base`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` and `xl` must stay; add your own, such as `{ id: "menu", label: "Menu folds", minWidth: 1081 }`. A breakpoint a draft node's style still names cannot go (422, with the node ids).

## layout.read

Read the site's layout frames as its draft resolves them: with `layoutId` (the frame a page names in `frame`, such as `default` or `scale-canvas`) that frame, without it every frame of the theme. Each comes as `{ layoutId, source, layout }`: `layout` is the whole frame object layout.update takes (its `frame` with `responsiveMode`, `designWidth` and `scaleFromWidth`, and the `header`, `footer`, `background`, `scroll`, `chrome` and `overridePolicy` layers), `source` is `site` when the site already replaced it with layout.update and `theme` when it is the theme's. Change the frame you read and send it whole to layout.update. A page may still override some layers for itself in `meta.layoutOverrides`; an unknown `layoutId` is layout_not_found (404).

- permission `site.read` (admin, editor); class `read`; writes nothing.

|---|---|---|
| `layoutId` | string (min 1) |  |

Example input:


## layout.update

Replace this site's version of one of the theme's layout frames (`layoutId`, the frame a page names in `frame`, such as `default` or `scale-canvas`) with `layout`, the whole frame object (its `id` is `layoutId`; read it first with layout.read, which answers it as the site resolves it now). `frame.responsiveMode` decides how its pages fit the window: `breakpoint` reflows them at the site breakpoints, with fluid tokens growing with the window; `scale` lays them out at `designWidth` and scales the whole canvas to the window from `scaleFromWidth` (769 px by default) up, reflowing below it. The other layers are `header`, `footer`, `background`, `scroll`, `chrome` and `overridePolicy` (which `meta.layoutOverrides` layers a page may apply). Colours and lengths are CSS, used as written: a token is its custom property, `var(--ds-color-bg-page)`; a `{color.bg.page}` reference is refused. Answers the frame as the site now resolves it, with warnings.

- permission `site.structure` (admin, workspace owner); class `transaction`; writes `settings`; undoable with `history.undo`.

## redirects.read

Read the draft redirects of the site: the list redirects.update replaces, each `{ from, to, status }`. The public site answers the redirects of its published version.

- permission `site.read` (admin, editor); class `read`; writes nothing.
- Input: `{}`.

Output: { redirects: ({ from: string (max 2048), to: string (max 2048), status: 301 \| 302 })[] (≤500) }

Example input:

```json
{}
```

## redirects.update

Replace the site's redirects with `redirects`, the whole list (at most 500; an empty list removes them all). Each rule is `{ from, to, status }`: `from` a path of this site, matched exactly with or without a trailing slash, or ending in `/*` to take that path and every path under it (`/old/*` takes `/old` and `/old/a/b`; an exact rule wins over a prefix, a longer prefix over a shorter one); `to` a path of this site (a query or a hash may follow; a request's query is kept when `to` has none) or an `https://` address; `status` 301 (moved for good) or 302 (moved for now). A locale's paths carry its prefix (`/en/old`). Refused with 422 `redirects_invalid`, every problem named: two rules with the same `from`, a loop (a target that a rule of the chain redirects again), or a rule that adds or changes a `from` on the path of a published page (unpublish the page or change its address first; an item path of a collection page is not checked). The platform's own paths (`/admin`, `/api`, `/_…`) are refused. Redirects are versioned: the public site answers them, before any page renders, after the next publish; undo restores the previous list.

- permission `site.edit` (admin, editor); class `transaction`; writes `settings`; undoable with `history.undo`.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `redirects` | ({ from: string (max 2048), to: string (max 2048), status: 301 \| 302 })[] (≤500) | yes |

Output: { redirects: ({ from: string (max 2048), to: string (max 2048), status: 301 \| 302 })[] (≤500) }

Example input:

```json
{"redirects":[{"from":"/old-about","to":"/about","status":301},{"from":"/shop/*","to":"https://shop.example.com/","status":302}]}
```

## environment.update

Replace the site's environment variables as a whole: `variables` maps each name to its new value, or to null to keep the stored value; a name left out is deleted, and null for a name with no stored value is refused. The input is redacted from the history and the audit log; undo restores the previous set.

- permission `site.admin` (admin); class `transaction`; writes `environment`; undoable with `history.undo`.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `variables` | Record<string, string \| null> | yes |

Output: { variables: Record<string, null> }

Example input:

```json
{"variables":{"NEWSLETTER_LIST_ID":"list-42"}}
```

## site.create

Create a new site in the program of this token's site, seeded from a blueprint (`blueprintId`, default `blank`: an empty home page with the theme's header and footer; the site's theme is the blueprint's). With `brand` (the brand.setup input), the new site's draft design system gets that brand in the same transaction, so the site is created branded or not at all. Answers the new site; this token stays scoped to its own site, so edit the new one with a token minted for it. Run it alone in a batch with the `site` base revision; it is not undoable (delete the site from the admin).

- permission `site.admin` (admin); class `transaction`; writes `site`; **not undoable**: alone in its batch.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string (min 1, max 255) | yes |
| `slug` | string (min 1, max 100) | yes |
| `blueprintId` | string (min 1, max 100) |  |
| `brand` | object |  |
| `brand.primary` | string | yes |
| `brand.secondary` | string | yes |
| `brand.neutral` | string | yes |
| `brand.headingFamily` | string (min 1)[] | yes |
| `brand.bodyFamily` | string (min 1)[] | yes |
| `brand.typeRatio` | 1.125 \| 1.2 \| 1.25 \| 1.333 | yes |
| `brand.baseSize` | integer ≥14 ≤22 | yes |
| `brand.spaceBase` | 4 \| 8 | yes |
| `brand.radius` | "sharp" \| "soft" \| "round" \| "pill" | yes |
| `defaultLocale` | locale |  |

Output: { site: { id: string, slug: string, name: string, theme: string, blueprintId: string, programId?: string, parentSiteId?: string \| null, mountPath?: string \| null, domain?: string, createdAt: string, updatedAt: string } }


## site.updateLanguages

Set the site's languages: the whole list (`locales`, 1 to 12 locale codes) and the default (`defaultLocale`, one of them). An added language changes only the list: pages show the default's text in it until translated. A removed language is swept out of every draft locale map (page fields and trees, menus, collections and items, site settings, forms, media texts); a value only that language had moves to the default. Removing a language needs `confirmed: ["destructive"]`; the current default cannot be removed (make another language the default first). A new default first gets the old default's value wherever it has none. Published versions change at the next publish. Answers the languages and, per removed language, how many values it lost or moved. Run it with the `site` base revision; it is not undoable.

- permission `site.admin` (admin); class `transaction`; writes `site`; **not undoable**: alone in its batch.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `locales` | locale[] (≤12) | yes |
| `defaultLocale` | locale | yes |

Output: { locales: locale[], defaultLocale: locale, removed: { locale: locale, values: integer ≥0 }[] }

Example input:

```json
{"locales":["it","fr"],"defaultLocale":"it"}
```

> Needs `site.admin`: only a platform admin's token. An editor or workspace owner asks a platform admin to add or remove a language.

## domain.add

Connect a hostname to the site. The platform's base domain or one plain label under it goes live at once; any other hostname waits for its DNS record (`ownershipVerification`, `dnsTarget`) and the edge provider's certificate, checked with domain.verify. The first domain under the platform domain that goes live becomes primary while the platform address still is. With `pair: true` a registrable domain or its www (`example.com`, `www.example.com`) connects both hostnames, answered as `domain` and `paired`; each verifies on its own, and the www becomes primary once it is live unless the site already has a custom primary, the apex then redirecting to it. Any other subdomain stays one hostname. A refused hostname is domain_refused with its `reason` (invalid, too_deep, platform_address, provider_unavailable; taken is 409). Site ownership is checked.

- permission `site.admin` (admin); class `external`; writes `site`; **not undoable**: alone in its batch; external: alone in its batch, never in a dry run.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `hostname` | string (min 1, max 255) | yes |
| `pair` | boolean |  |

Output: { domain: { id: string, siteId: string, hostname: string, kind: "platform" \| "custom", isPrimary: boolean, redirectToPrimary: boolean, status: "pending" \| "active" \| "error", dnsStatus: string, provider: string \| null, providerId: string \| null, providerStatus: string \| null, sslStatus: string \| null, dnsTarget: string… (full schema: discover_operations)

Example input:

```json
{"hostname":"www.example.com"}
```

|---|---|---|
| `domainId` | uuid | yes |

Example input:

```json
{"domainId":"9c0d1e2f-3a4b-4c5d-9e6f-7a8b9c0d1e2f"}
```

## domain.delete

Disconnect a domain from the site and release it at the edge provider; the platform address cannot be removed. With `pair: true` the other hostname of its pair (its apex or its www) goes too. When the primary goes, the platform address takes over. Site ownership is checked.

- permission `site.admin` (admin); class `external`; writes `site`; needs `"confirmed": ["destructive"]`; **not undoable**: alone in its batch; external: alone in its batch, never in a dry run.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `domainId` | uuid | yes |
| `pair` | boolean |  |

Output: { success: true }

Example input:

```json
{"domainId":"9c0d1e2f-3a4b-4c5d-9e6f-7a8b9c0d1e2f"}
```

## maintenance.migrate

Bring the draft page trees in line with the theme's component props: a prop removed or retyped since the site's last props snapshot is stripped from every draft tree, all pages or none, after a backup of the trees it changes (an added prop writes nothing). A publish runs the same step. It runs in one transaction and is not undone: recovery is maintenance.restoreBackup.

- permission `site.admin` (admin); class `transaction`; writes `pages`, `site`; needs `"confirmed": ["destructive"]`; **not undoable**: alone in its batch.
- Input: `{}`.

Output: { auto: Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (… \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …)[] \| Record<string, … \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …>> \| null }

Example input:

```json
{}
```

## maintenance.restoreBackup

Restore the draft page trees a migration backup holds (`backupId`): each page's root children go back to the backup's, in one commit for all the pages. It runs in one transaction and is not undone: recovery is maintenance.restoreBackup.

- permission `site.admin` (admin); class `transaction`; writes `pages`, `site`; needs `"confirmed": ["destructive"]`; **not undoable**: alone in its batch.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `backupId` | string (min 1) | yes |

Output: { success: true, restoredCount: integer ≥0, pageCount: integer ≥0 }

Example input:

```json
{"backupId":"backup-2026-10-16"}
```
